chunks.title: [Master Express Lesson 3] Complete Guide to CLO Rendering Materials - Recorded Session is Here~
chunks.content: ## Overview of CLO Rendering Materials and Their Applications This section covers the various types of materials available in CLO for rendering, including hair loss types, fabric materials, and their reflective properties. It also explains how to apply these materials within the 3D environment to achieve realistic fabric and object appearances. ### Hair Loss Types in CLO CLO provides a variety of hair loss types to simulate fabric texture details: - **Default Hair Loss**: The standard type used for general purposes. - **Total Types**: 12 hair loss types are available. - **Render Only Types**: 5 hair loss types labeled "REND ONLY," visible only during rendering. Users can select hair loss types according to their needs to enhance realism in fabric textures. ### Material Types and Their Representations CLO includes multiple material presets that represent different fabric and object surface properties: - **Matte**: Reflects the characteristics of a normal plant surface with minimal shine. - **Shiny**: Represents surfaces with a glossy, reflective finish. - **Silk**: Simulates the subtle glow and reflective quality of silk fabric. - **Diamond Effect**: Mimics the sparkle of diamond surfaces. - **Glass**: Used for transparent or semi-transparent glass surfaces with reflection and refraction properties. - **Glitter**: Adds sparkling particle effects to surfaces. - **Light Effect**: Simulates light emission or glow. - **Leather**: Represents the texture and reflectivity of leather. - **Plastic**: Simulates plastic surfaces with typical reflectivity and roughness. Each material can be customized by adjusting parameters like color, surface roughness, reflection intensity, and transparency. ## Applying Silk Material on Fabric in CLO This section explains how to apply and customize the silk material on fabric objects in CLO to achieve realistic silk textures and color effects. ### Procedure for Applying Silk Material 1. Open the **Fabric 1** tab in the object window. 2. Select the silk fabric provided in the fabric storage. 3. Drag and drop the silk fabric onto the target garment piece, such as a skirt. 4. Alternatively, select the fabric and set the attribute type to "silk." ### Adjusting Silk Material Properties - **Color Adjustment**: Change the fabric color to better visualize the silk effect; for example, switching to blue enhances the silk's gloss. - **Front Color Strength**: Controls the saturation of the primary color on the fabric surface. - Higher value results in more saturated color. - Adjust to balance between color intensity and silk texture realism. - **Side Color Strength**: Defines the color of the fabric edges. - Higher values increase edge reflections, enhancing the silk glow. - **Surface Roughness**: Determines the smoothness of the fabric surface. - Silk generally has high surface roughness to simulate its texture. - Lower roughness values create a smoother, less textured surface. - **Reflection Intensity**: Controls how much light the fabric reflects. - Silk fabric usually has low reflection intensity to mimic its subtle glow. Adjusting these parameters allows fine-tuning of the silk fabric's appearance in the 3D render.

Besides hair, there are many other materials in CLO that can render stunning effects~  
Future CLO masters, are you ready to master rendering~~

Adjusting these parameters allows fine-tuning of the silk fabric's appearance in the 3D render. ## Creating Metallic Effects on Accessories This section describes how to create metallic textures on objects like belts within CLO using the material editor, including color changes and reflection settings. ### Steps to Create Metal Material 1. Select the target object (e.g., a belt) in the 3D window. 2. Open the material editor to analyze and edit the object's material. 3. Apply a metallic feel by adjusting: - **Color**: Change from silver to gold by adjusting the color to yellow hues. - **Surface Roughness**: Controls smoothness; smoother surfaces give a shinier metal look. - **Reflection**: Metals have high reflection; ensure reflection is enabled and properly adjusted. 4. Observe reflections during rotation to verify metallic appearance. Proper adjustment of these settings results in realistic metallic surfaces that respond dynamically to light. ## Glass Material Settings and Transparency Control This section covers how to apply glass materials to objects, manage transparency, reflection, and surface roughness to simulate realistic glass effects in CLO. ### Applying Glass Material - Assign the glass material to the desired object (e.g., a chest component). - Enable static and synchronized reflections to activate reflective properties. - Adjust parameters: - **Surface Roughness**: Lower values make the glass surface smoother. - **Reflection Intensity**: Higher values increase the reflectivity of the glass. - **Absorption Value**: Controls transparency; smaller values make the glass more transparent. ### Transparency and Visual Effects - Setting the absorption value to around 0.1 creates a highly transparent glass, allowing background colors or objects to be seen through. - Increasing absorption to 10 reduces transparency while maintaining reflective surface qualities. - The glass effect is visible in the 3D window but not in the 2D window, where the material appears as a semi-transparent pink color by default. Fine-tuning these parameters allows for realistic glass rendering, simulating both transparency and reflective properties. ## Creating Pearl-like Buttons and Thread Effects This section explains how to simulate pearl buttons and thread effects using material properties in CLO. ### Pearl Buttons - Select the button object and apply a silk material attribute to simulate pearl gloss. - Adjust: - **Surface Roughness**: Lower values make the button surface smoother. - **Reflection Intensity**: Increase to enhance the pearl-like shine. - Customize button color for desired pearl hues. ### Thread Effects - Select the thread attribute (e.g., SuMiao type). - Apply a darker gray color. - Adjust transparency (e.g., set to 10) to mimic the look of hot glue or semi-transparent thread. - These settings create realistic thread appearances in the garment rendering.

chunks.content: ### Pearl Buttons - Select the button object and apply a silk material attribute to simulate pearl gloss. - Adjust: - **Surface Roughness**: Lower values make the button surface smoother. - **Reflection Intensity**: Increase to enhance the pearl-like shine. - Customize button color for desired pearl hues. ### Thread Effects - Select the thread attribute (e.g., SuMiao type). - Apply a darker gray color. - Adjust transparency (e.g., set to 10) to mimic the look of hot glue or semi-transparent thread. - These settings create realistic thread appearances in the garment rendering. ## Adding Glitter Effects to Fabrics This section details how to apply and control glitter particle effects on fabrics, including particle count, color variation, and color randomization. ### Applying Glitter 1. Select the fabric of the garment (e.g., a dress). 2. Change the glitter color in the editor to match design requirements. 3. Enable the mirror window and synchronization rendering for real-time preview. ### Controlling Glitter Particles - **Particle Count**: Adjusts the number of glitter particles visible. - Higher counts (e.g., 300) produce a denser glitter effect. - Lower counts (e.g., 30) reduce glitter density for subtle sparkle. - **Color Randomization**: - Set to 0 for uniform color of glitter particles. - Set to 1 for random multi-color glitter effects. - **RGB Values**: - Adjust RGB values to customize the base color of glitter. - Closer RGB values result in more color variation. - Maximize one color channel for single-color glitter effects. This functionality allows precise customization of glitter appearance to fit various garment designs. ## Rendering Settings and Visual Results This section explains key rendering parameters for fabrics and materials and presents the effects achieved through rendering in CLO. ### Important Rendering Parameters - **Surface Roughness**: Affects smoothness and texture visibility. - **Reflection Intensity**: Controls light reflection level on materials. - **Absorption Value**: Adjusts transparency, especially relevant for glass materials. - **Depth Value**: Relates to object thickness and affects transparency perception. - **Contrast Value**: Modifies depth-related contrast effects in rendering. - **Opacity Value**: Controls the visibility of materials in the render. ### Rendering Outcomes - Silk materials show increased light reflection and a glowing effect. - Metallic objects reflect light realistically with variable colors (silver, gold). - Glass materials demonstrate transparency and reflective qualities based on absorption and roughness settings. - Pearl buttons and hot glue threads have distinct reflective and transparency characteristics. - Glitter effects display varying sparkle intensity and color randomness according to settings. Rendered images provide detailed views of fabric textures, transparency, and reflective properties for quality assurance. ## Additional Notes and FAQs This section addresses common questions and clarifications related to materials and rendering in CLO. ### Light and Lamp Objects - Lamps and light bulbs in CLO are typically OBJ-type secondary objects imported from other 3D software. - Their physical attributes cannot be changed within CLO, only their appearance. - Lighting effects on lamps are achieved by turning on their power in the scene.
